name: Kiln — Creative Technology Studio
description: A near-black, technology-led creative studio site whose home page is the work itself: every project as a cell on the inside of a sphere — the middle flat and far, the edges tilting in — that you drag in any direction, forever, drifting when nobody holds it. It opens on a canvas intro where the studio's vessel mascot arrives out of big pixels, is fired through five glazes in hard cuts and blows away as dust. A grid/list switch turns the wall into a year-by-year index with a cursor-following preview, and a filter panel sets the disciplines as one loud sentence. Below: a word-by-word manifesto, a pinned stage of three working devices (a glaze-firing web toy, a field-recording phone app, a billboard you write), oversized selected work, count-ups, a partner marquee and a closing ask in a border beam — plus Studio (stacking process cards, team, live studio clocks), Careers (filterable roles, an application sheet with CV drop), case studies, a real sound switch and a live brand guide.
designedFor: Creative agencies, design studios and production houses showing a large body of work
Portfolios that want the work to be the home page — a draggable, curved, endless project wall
Dark, editorial sites with oversized golden-ratio type and mono labels
Seeing a canvas intro, sticky scroll stories and working device mockups built as editor-controllable components
